To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with advanced nonsquamous NSLC should be offered cisplatin/pemtrexed chemotherapy, patients with EGFR mutation should be offered EGFR-tyrosine-kinase-inhibitor therapy and patients with ERCC1 overexpression should be offered nonplatinum chemotherapy.

* In advanced nonsquamous NS-CLC, cisplatin plus pemetrexed is superior to cisplatin plus gemcitabine or vinorelbine, and * In advanced NS-CLC with EGFR mutations, gefitinib is superior to standard chemotherapy.
the treatment of advanced nonsquamous NS-CLC should be cisplatin/pem- etrexed, and the treatment of EGFR mutation positive NS-CLC with gefitinib.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to improve treatment for patients with advanced nonsquamous NSLCC and EGFR mutation positive NSCLC.
the identification of the best possible treatment options for patients with lung cancer.
the identification of new treatment strategies for patients with NSCLC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of biomarkers in the treatment of advanced NSCLC is a reality in the daily practice of oncology.
treatment with cisplatin and pemetrexed is the standard first line chemotherapy for advanced NSCLC patients with non-squamous cell histology.
the best treatment of NSCLC is a combination of the right patient, the right drug and the right dose at the right time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment of advanced NSCLC has evolved to the point where the individual patient is considered and not just his tumour.

the treatment of advanced NSCLC is now tailored according to histology, EGFR mutation status, and possibly also ERCC1 or betatubulin expression, and that this approach has been shown to improve outcome in randomised trials and in retrospective analysis.
we have shown the importance of tailored treatment in advanced NSCLCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to improve outcome for patients with advanced NSCLC by tailoring treatment according either to histological subtypes or to biomarkers.
the use of biomarkers to guide therapy is a reality today, with a number of biomarker-based trials ongoing.
treatment of advanced NSCLC can be tailored to the individual patient.
